author: Spinazz27
quote:
Pokémon Z-A is a big disappointment. The story feels lazy and uninspired, with almost no emotional depth or interesting characters. The soundtrack is forgettable — nothing compared to the older generations. The map is also surprisingly small and empty, making exploration feel boring and repetitive. For a series that used to feel magical, this one just feels flat and rushed. 

I really wanted to like Pokémon Z-A, but honestly, it’s one of the weakest entries in the entire series. The game feels soulless from start to finish. The story is extremely flat — there’s no real motivation, no charm, and none of the emotional punch that older Pokémon games used to deliver. The characters are bland, the dialogue is dull, and the pacing is painfully slow.

The music is another huge letdown. It lacks personality and energy, almost like it was made for background noise instead of an actual adventure. Older Pokémon games had iconic themes that stuck in your head — this one doesn’t. Most tracks sound generic, repetitive, and uninspired.

The map is small, empty, and lifeless. There’s barely anything to explore, and what little there is feels copy-pasted. For a game that was supposed to be “next-gen,” it feels more like a step backward. Even side areas feel rushed, with little reward or reason to revisit them.

Graphically, it’s fine, but nothing impressive for 2025 standards. The visuals don’t make up for the lack of atmosphere. The performance isn’t great either, with small stutters and long loading times that ruin the immersion.

Overall, Pokémon Z-A feels like a missed opportunity. It could have been something special — especially after so much hype — but instead, it’s just another rushed and empty release. The magic is gone.
